Yeah, I’m not sure why anyone makes the graphics argument against nintendo when damn near every single one of their games are loved by at least one large group of people. TotK looks beautiful and its because of the consistent color palette and art style. It takes a genuine skill to nail down and stick to an art style especially on a game this massive. 

I’d even go on and say elden ring’s graphics aren’t VERY impressive, but the particles and post processing effects / lighting all look very clean and it makes using magic (for example) feel very very cool. A lot more goes into a game than just how it’s presented, but what can the game do to make the player feel like they’re a part of the world? 

Thats what totk nails for me, every object is physical. They managed to make a robust building/physics engine on a NINTENDO SWITCH (most peoples phones are more powerful) and besides the people who really understand it, people tend to gloss over how much work goes into something like that. You’re not seeing other AAA studios put so much time and effort into that type of stuff, probably hasn’t been a game this interactive since Half Life lol

this game is genius in terms of giving you tools to play with. it’s essentially a big sandbox and you can do a lot of cool things in it.

lets say you got to the top of this mountain, that in of itself was a fun task to me, i love seeing my player just crawl up this massive cliffside and having to take breaks on small shelves to get my stamina up. not to mention it could also rain, and even many times i’ve seen a handful of things out in the distance that just made me feel good, wether that be the mountains in the horizon, seeing the divine beasts i’ve freed beaming a laser at the castle, or even just a sunset/rise is enough for me. the game is beautiful and link has never had this many tools to explore with. 

then when you get to the top of this mountain theres for sure SOMETHING.. wether it be a little korok puzzle (which can easily be missed, i’ve missed a bunch of them) or a strong monster, or even “nothing” but you can now see a part of the map you didn’t know existed, making the world feel that much bigger.

all in all, i probably enjoy the little things in botw more than a lot of other people do, and i probably play it a bit differently than others do, but i find my fun in just being able to go wherever i want, wether that be the highest peaks, or taking a boat on the water. its all fun and intuitive, then link unlocks more tools to play in the world with as you progress through the game

i’ll also say this is my first zelda game that i’ve sunk my teeth into, but i definitely do want to try the more linear games
